review_comments: Are we preferring fields as opposed to properties? If we are going with non-private fields I think I'd prefer them to not start with an `_` prefix. Unsure if this is a common pattern or not.
Using properties would allow us to set the property to non `null` and hide that away instead of it leaking to other places.

> I think I'd prefer them to not start with an _ prefix.

The libraries [coding style](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/docs/coding-guidelines/coding-style.md) is to use `_` prefix for both private and internal fields.

> Are we preferring fields as opposed to properties

Have no strong preference, used the same pattern already or other internal types, can change to property if needed.

> Using properties would allow us to set the property to non null and hide that away instead of it leaking to other places.

Not sure I understood, but the null value is used for deciding if they should be emitted
Okay. This is slightly more nuanced than I thought. Let's leave it.
nit: whitespace seems a bit off;  Add linefeed before comment + before `int i =0`.
Where did these max values come from?
Yes, compiler warns otherwise, by my understanding this is because `MetadataBuilder` (and `BlobBuilder`) is not  CLSCompliant, why do you think it is not appropriate?
There is nothing in this signature that is obviously not compliant. It is fine if the compiler is complaining.

> It is fine if the compiler is complaining

It is not a warning it is an error, so build fails without the attribute: 
`Error	CS3001	Argument type 'BlobBuilder' is not CLS-compliant	System.Reflection.Emit`
Can we use the `SequencePoint.Hidden` constant here instead?
I think it would be helpful to indicate in a `<remarks>` section that the arguments have already been validated. Unsure if this is the common assumption for this API style.
